scope: Theorem 14.4 (Original-data exterior rigidity) of the manuscript “Equality and rigidity in the spacetime Penrose inequality” (preprints/Equality-and-rigidity-in-the-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f1aab59ba484eb8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 118. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (Ω, g, K) belong to Definition 14.3, and set m = √︂ E2 − |P|2 δ. Then m = 1 2 (︃ A ω )︃2/3 (14.7) if and only if the original initial data admit a global smooth spacelike embedding, including S, into the regular maximal extension of gm. The image lies in the closure of the corresponding exterior, its end approaches that spatial infinity, and S maps to a smooth section of its future horizon or to its bifurcation sphere. The induced metric is the original g, and its second fundamental form for a consistent future unit normal is the original K with convention (14.1). The embedding and normal are smooth up to S in regular horizon coordinates. Equivalently, every such hypersurface in gM0 satisfying Definition 14.3 and the prescribed asymptotic assumptions has invariant ADM mass M0, horizon area ω(2M0)3/2, and equality in (14.5).
